availability.text: Available now for full-time Solutions Architect, Technical Account Manager or engineering leadership roles. Remote across Europe, or hybrid in Milan or Turin. EU citizen, no sponsorship required.

bio: I work where business intent meets engineering reality. Since 2011, without a gap, that has meant endpoint engineering at a Renault plant, back-end work on the Disney Parks checkout, and modernising a core banking team at BBVA.

At Toptal I ran the whole client lifecycle on my own: discovery calls, architecture and stack assessment, matching, rate negotiation and replacements. When a delivery was contested, I was the one who read the code and wrote the finding that settled it.

Since 2026 I build AI tools hands-on and advise founders on scope and feasibility for AI products: what is worth building, what is not, and what it costs to run at production volume rather than at pilot volume.
I live in Manta, in Piedmont, and work with teams across Europe.

projects.title: Artemis Quiver
projects.description: Chrome extension and web app that scores a job posting against your CV, then drafts a tailored CV and cover letter with the LLM of your choice, cloud or local. No backend and no account: your data stays in your browser.
projects.problem: Tailoring a CV to every posting is slow, and pasting a whole career history into a hosted chatbot gives it away.
projects.role: Sole developer: product, architecture, code, tests and releases. I built it for my own job search and use it every day.
projects.outcome: Open source, at v3.9.4 with 147 commits, an automated test suite in CI and versioned GitHub releases (October 2026).
projects.stack: React 18, Vite, Tailwind, Chrome MV3, Dexie on IndexedDB. LLM providers behind one adapter: OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini and in-browser WebLLM.

image.alt: Artemis Quiver's Job Analysis screen: a 92% match score with reasoning, interview preparation tips and CV suggestions for a sample profile.

projects.aiNote: Built with AI coding agents. A project AGENTS.md file records the architecture decisions and forbidden patterns; I set the direction, review every change and own the tests.

projects.title: Artemis Flow
projects.description: Job-discovery pipeline that reads a plain-language profile and has a local LLM write the search strategy (keywords, locations, exclusions) instead of relying on static filters. It feeds Quiver over REST. Private repository.
projects.problem: Job boards are full of duplicates and near-misses, and a keyword filter cannot say what a good fit looks like.
projects.role: Sole developer, from the ingestion design to the scoring experiments.
projects.outcome: Ingests from job boards, ATS APIs and 28 company career pages, merges duplicates on requisition identity rather than text similarity, and scores every job with a rationale. Runs on local models at no API cost.
projects.stack: Python, FastAPI, SQLite, Playwright, React; Ollama and LM Studio for local inference.

projects.title: Local LLM infrastructure
projects.description: A Raspberry Pi gateway fronts a desktop compute node with Nginx and can wake it over the LAN, so my other projects run on self-hosted models instead of paid APIs.
projects.stack: Raspberry Pi, Nginx, Wake-on-LAN, Ollama, Docker Compose.

experience.summary: Advise founders in my network on AI adoption and on scope and feasibility for AI products. Build AI tooling hands-on: Artemis Quiver and Artemis Flow.

Ran the full client lifecycle solo across 200+ SMB and mid-market clients, from discovery and stack assessment to matching, rate negotiation and replacements. Designed the technical discovery framework that lifted placements from 30% to 70%. Acted as technical arbiter in contested engagements, auditing delivered code in Rust, Python, R and PHP.

Hired to modernise a team whose engineers had twenty years' tenure and no version control. Introduced Scrum, git and a Bitbucket, Jenkins and SonarQube pull-request pipeline that took deployments from days to minutes under banking compliance, and started the move from Java 5/6 and VB8 to Java 8 and Spring Boot while keeping access to the COBOL core.

Maintained checkout microservices for Disney Parks e-commerce at 99.9% uptime through peak seasonal load. On the Equifax account, contributed to the technical definition and proposal for a post-breach migration of encryption services to GCP, without implementation.

Single point of contact for the 2017 WannaCry response: 1,000+ endpoints isolated and patched over a 48-hour weekend, and the plant was in full production on Monday. Owned the plant's software standards and cut Level 2 escalations by about 30% with PowerShell automation and a shared knowledge base.

posts.description: Checking the artifact, not the announcement: a benchmark scored with refusal switched off, a five-tool ceiling that changed my router design, and a perfectly reproducible scorer that had no scoring value.
